title: SG-7.6 · Runner locking, timeout, retry, budget and approval gate unit tests
summary: Prove Runner.Run lock, timeout, retry, budget and cleanup behavior with unit tests, including a real ErrTimeout
description: Context: backend/worker/internal/runner/runner.go already implements the per-World lock, per-attempt timeout, retry loop, ErrBudgetExceeded and worktree cleanup, and many tests exist. Gaps: no exported ErrTimeout exists (a timeout surfaces only as context.DeadlineExceeded), and nothing proves a timed-out agent is retried once and then FAILED. Desired behavior: Run returns an error wrapping ErrTimeout when an attempt times out, and unit tests prove lock-held, timeout retry, MaxRetries exhaustion with single worktree removal, and budget stop. Why: the worker must fail predictably and never leave stray worktrees.
acceptance_criteria: Given the lock file is already held, When Run is called, Then the error wraps lock.ErrLocked, the agent never runs and no worktree is created
Given the agent blocks past Timeout and MaxRetries is 1, When Run is called, Then the agent runs twice, the stored status is FAILED and the error wraps ErrTimeout
Given every attempt fails and MaxRetries is 2, When Run is called, Then the agent runs 3 times, the stored status is FAILED and the worktree is removed exactly once
Given each failed attempt costs 3.0, MaxBudget is 5.0 and MaxRetries is 5, When Run is called, Then the error wraps ErrBudgetExceeded after 2 agent runs and the stored status is FAILED

in_scope: Runner unit tests with fake agent, worktrees, publisher, store in temp dir and fixed clock
out_of_scope: Real Git worktrees or real Claude CLI
preserve: Budget check semantics (zero or negative budget unlimited)

technical_constraints: Go tests only, no network, no real processes
Use existing fakes in runner_test.go (fakeAgent, fakeTrees, newRunner)
definition_of_done: All four acceptance criteria are asserted by passing unit tests
non_functional: Tests finish in under a second using a 20ms timeout
